principles: Memory remains advisory and never gate evidence.
Correctness parity is required before any performance claim.
Reuse existing B-ec3b index and pack builder semantics instead of replacing runtime memory.
Keep M3-M6 mechanically verifiable with one dedicated smoke plus existing baselines.
drivers: Need optimized entry-layer memory without overclaiming million-record runtime speed.
Need cache and consumer rollout to preserve current facts over memory.
Need M6 report-first latency split for reference/indexed/cached paths.

options.name: A: shared optimized pack API plus cache module
pros: Centralizes advisory boundary and cache key semantics
Makes M5/M6 parity easier to test
cons: Requires careful options plumbing through existing consumers

options.name: B: per-consumer cache wiring
cons: Higher drift risk and more places to accidentally change authority semantics

chosen: A: shared optimized pack API plus cache module
rationale: Choose the shared optimized pack API because M3-M6 are about one consistent runtime memory entry layer. A central cache/key/freshness path makes it easier to prove gateEvidence=false, parity, and invalidation across consumers.

preMortem.scenario: Cache returns stale or irrelevant memory as fresh
preMortem.trigger: Cache key omits contributing source digest, policy, limits, or indexVersion
preMortem.consequence: Hosts see stale lessons and repeat past errors
preMortem.mitigation: Include those fields in cache key and add stale-relevant/stale-irrelevant negative tests.

preMortem.scenario: Optimized path changes semantics from reference path
preMortem.trigger: Candidate prefilter drops required rows or mishandles supersession
preMortem.consequence: Runtime memory becomes faster but less reliable
preMortem.mitigation: M5 matrix and M6 parity compare required ids, false-surface, supersession, deprecated residue, malformed rows, maxLines, and omittedCount.

preMortem.trigger: Small fixture cache hit is mistaken for 1M indexed/cached hot path
preMortem.consequence: Paper/docs or host response claims unsupported 1-2s million runtime
preMortem.mitigation: No-overclaim rule remains in docs and M6 must report latency separately without enforcing SLO before correctness parity is green.
